title: Boot — desktop 1280×800
attestation: Desktop boot of the real preview bundle. Top-left: 'ORE 3' in signal-yellow beside two empty yellow-outlined cargo slots. Top-centre: 'WAVE 1/5 · Outer Drift', 'NEXT 2:29' in cyan, 'MATCH 0:02' in grey. Screen centre: a small steel triangle ship pointing left with a blue cockpit dot (the placeholder ship). Six grey filled circles (asteroids) are scattered down the left third. Bottom edge: the full controls strip — 'WASD Thrust · Mouse Aim · Left mouse Fire / Mine · E Build & Upgrade · Space / Shift Boost · Middle click Ping'. Bottom-right corner: the build stamp '4bb8a15 · 18:29Z'. No error overlay. This proves the client boots to a playable frame on desktop.

title: Boot — emulated phone, landscape 844×390
attestation: Boot on an emulated iPhone-class device (844×390, dpr 3, touch) held landscape. Same HUD as desktop — 'ORE 3' + two cargo slots top-left, 'WAVE 1/5 · Outer Drift / NEXT 2:29 / MATCH 0:02' top-centre, steel triangle ship centred. Touch affordances are drawn unprompted: a thin cyan idle ring (the left thumb-stick home) bottom-left, and a cyan-ringed circular 'FIRE' button bottom-right. Build stamp '4bb8a15 · 18:29Z' bottom-right. The controls-strip text is not shown on the phone (touch layer owns the bottom), which is correct. Proves the client boots and lays out for a landscape phone with the touch UI present.

title: HUD — live, running match (desktop)
attestation: Desktop HUD after ~7 s of live (un-frozen) play. The wave clock reads 'NEXT 2:24 / MATCH 0:07' — advanced from the 'NEXT 2:29 / MATCH 0:02' seen at boot, so the clock is genuinely counting, not a still. 'ORE 3' + two cargo slots top-left; controls strip along the bottom. This is the three HUD elements the brief asks for together in one live frame: the ore squares, the wave clock, and the controls strip.

Drawn unprompted: a thin cyan idle ring in the lower-left (the dynamic left thumb-stick's home position) and a cyan-ringed 'FIRE' button in the lower-right. attestation: Emulated phone, landscape, with a synthetic touch pointer pressed and dragged in the lower-left. A filled translucent-cyan disc (the stick knob) now sits at the upper-right edge of the left-stick ring — the knob has moved off centre toward the drag, i.e. the dynamic stick is tracking the thumb. The 'FIRE' button remains cyan-ringed in the lower-right. Proves the ghost/thumb-stick responds to touch, not just that its idle ring is drawn.

title: ROTATE overlay — portrait, iOS-Safari capability profile
attestation: Emulated iPhone-class phone held PORTRAIT (390×844), with screen.orientation.lock removed before boot to emulate the iOS-Safari profile the overlay is gated to (it only shows where orientation lock is unavailable). A full-screen overlay is drawn: a cyan phone-with-curved-arrow rotate glyph, 'ROTATE YOUR DEVICE' in bold cyan, and 'Planet Rush plays in landscape' beneath it. The game HUD is dimmed behind. Proves the portrait ROTATE overlay renders on the platform it targets.

title: Portrait on lock-capable Chromium (overlay correctly absent)
attestation: The SAME portrait phone WITHOUT the capability stub — stock headless Chromium, which reports orientation-lock support. The ROTATE overlay is NOT shown; the normal portrait game renders instead (centred ship, 'ORE 3', idle left-stick ring, 'FIRE' button, wave clock). This is the specified behaviour — a lock-capable platform takes the lock path, not the overlay — so this shot does NOT prove the overlay; it documents that the gate is real. The overlay itself is proven by rotate-overlay-portrait-ios. Marked inconclusive for the overlay claim.

title: GATE: 8-planet ring on screen
attestation: Re-captured on the wired build (PR #40, m2-wire-the-war). Seeded ?debug=1&freeze=1 world, viewport widened to 3600×2000 so the 1:1 follow-camera can reach the whole ring (planets sit ~896 world-px from the arena centre, the far one ~1702 px from the local ship it centres on). ON SCREEN: EIGHT planet bodies arranged in a ring around a central cluster of grey asteroids (the field). Each planet is a dark patina disc with a signal-yellow core and two teal segments, encircled by a distinct owner beacon ring — I count eight different colours (white/grey top-centre, orange upper-left, blue upper-right, magenta far-left, blue right, purple lower-left, teal lower-right, green bottom-centre) — and each has its own small ship triangle beside it. HUD reads 'WAVE 1/5 · Outer Drift / NEXT 2:28 / MATCH 0:02', 'ORE 3', 'HOME' top-right. This is the full 8-planet ring, rendered. PASSES the gate.

title: GATE: Build wheel open with costs
attestation: Re-captured on the wired build. Held 'E' (the strip's 'E Build & Upgrade' binding) while docked at the ship's spawn planet. ON SCREEN: the Build & Upgrade wheel is OPEN — a radial ring of FIVE labelled segments around a hub. Reading clockwise from twelve o'clock: 'TURRET / YOUR PLANET' with cost '3'; 'SHIELD / YOUR PLANET' cost '5'; 'REPAIR CORE / YOUR PLANET' cost '1'; 'UPGRADE SHIP / YOUR SHIP' (highlighted, with a ▶ pointer and no cost — it opens the upgrade panel); 'BANK / YOUR PLANET' (no cost). The hub prints the live ore total '3 · ORE' inside a cyan selection ring. A tooltip banner reads 'Spend ore on defense — or UPGRADE SHIP to mine and hit harder' (the SPEND onboarding lesson). Build stamp 'c97f60a · 21:44Z' bottom-right. The wheel is open and its costs — 3, 5, 1 — are the only numbers on the wedges, exactly as GDD §2.5 specifies. PASSES the gate.

title: GATE: turret mid-construction
attestation: Re-captured on the wired build. Opened the wheel (hold E), clicked the TURRET wedge at twelve o'clock to place the order, closed the wheel (hold E again) to unobscure the planet, then let the 10 s build (TURRET.buildTime) run partway. ON SCREEN: the home planet (dark disc, blue owner beacon ring, yellow core, teal segments) carries a build-progress overlay — a faint full steel ring at the planet's edge with a bright plasma-cyan arc drawn over it, starting at twelve o'clock and sweeping clockwise about two-thirds of the way round, with an open gap in the upper-left. No completed turret stands on the rim yet, so the arc is mid-build, not done. 'ORE' now reads '0' — down from the '3' it showed before the order — i.e. the turret's cost-3 was spent to queue this build. HUD 'WAVE 1/5 · Outer Drift / NEXT 2:23 / MATCH 0:08', stamp 'c97f60a · 21:44Z'. A turret is visibly under construction on the planet. PASSES the gate. (Manifest id renamed from the prior 'turret-under-construction' to 'turret-construction' to match the M2 gate key.)

title: GATE: under-attack alarm arrow
attestation: Re-captured on the wired build. The prior caveat — 'offline there is no attacker' — no longer holds: the seven rivals are live bots (match-boot.ts), and leaving your home undefended draws one onto the core within seconds. Method: held 'A' to thrust toward the arena centre so home recedes off the right edge, and gated the shutter on the sim's own tick counter (window.__planetRush.ticks ≥ 1200) rather than wall time. A headless replay of this exact input confirms the alarm fires from ~tick 790 with the core alive past tick 2000, so this frame sits inside a real siege. ON SCREEN, at 'MATCH 0:21': the under-attack ALARM is firing — a threat-red frame around the screen edges (pulsing, so faint at this instant but visible along the top edge and corners) and, decisively, the alarm's own banner 'Your planet is under attack — follow the arrow' (ui/onboarding.ts, shown only while the alarm is active). A threat-red screen-edge ARROW sits at the right edge pointing right — toward the home planet, which is off-screen to the right because I flew away. The local ship (blue triangle) is centred out in the field beside a rival's planet (centre, shown with a threat-red damage ring — a scouted enemy home, not mine), with other bot ships nearby. Alarm + directional home arrow, during an actual attack. PASSES the gate.

title: Field bug m2-10: enemy beam visible mid-attack
attestation: Re-verified on the CURRENT live build 0a3a313 — HEAD of main after the m2-15/m2-16 wiring landed (PRs #60, #61), rebuilt locally (dist stamp sha 0a3a313, clean tree). Staged deterministically through the ?debug=1&freeze=1 seams the wiring fix ships: __healthbarStage.damageEnemy(0.4) parks the first non-local bot 120 world-px right of the centred local ship, then __planetRush.stageCombat() publishes that same bot's beam; freeze pins the sim so the staged beam is never stepped away before the shutter. The image is the 1900×1100 frame zoomed 3× (full frame committed as images/combat-staged.png). WHAT IS ON SCREEN: the parked enemy bot sits at the home planet's right edge, and a CYAN beam (the non-local shooter's colour) runs from it rightward and ENDS clamped on a filled hit-dot — an enemy laser, drawn, terminating at its strike point. The local ship (the grey triangle left of the planet) is NOT firing this frame, so this beam is unambiguously non-local, not my own control beam. Corroborated at the instrument: __planetRush.beams reports exactly TWO drawn beams, BOTH shooter:1 (non-local) — one source:'ship' (this beam, origin (1886.4,960) → end/hit (2026.4,960)) and one source:'turret' — where the round-2 evidence found ZERO non-local beams in-frame. The round-2 failure was that main.ts fed the renderer only LOCAL_PLAYER's beam; main.ts now builds currentBeams() from combatBeams(world), one record per firing emitter, so every shooter draws. VERIFIED: enemy lasers are visible in the booted client.

title: Field bug m2-12: friendly turret visibly firing
attestation: Re-verified on live build 0a3a313. Staged through __planetRush.stageCombat() under ?debug=1&freeze=1, which mounts a turret with a live muzzle on a NON-LOCAL planet and publishes its shot; captured at 3600×2000 (the proven planet-ring width) so the 1:1 follow-camera frames that rival planet, shown zoomed 2.5× (full ring: images/turret-muzzle.png, all 8 owner-beacon rings visible). WHAT IS ON SCREEN: on the rim of a teal-beacon-ringed planet sits the turret — a small grey body — and from it a CYAN MUZZLE BEAM rises straight up to a filled hit-dot: a turret visibly loosing a shot, the exact tell round-2 found invisible. (The second, horizontal cyan beam beside it is the staged enemy SHIP beam from an adjacent bot.) Corroborated at the instrument: __planetRush.beams carries a source:'turret', shooter:1 record, origin world (1593.6,1517.6) → end (1593.6,1427.6), which projects to screen (1627,1558)→(1627,1468) — exactly where the vertical beam is drawn. HONEST SCOPE: the deterministic stager mounts the turret on a non-local (rival) planet, so this is a rival turret's muzzle, not a friendly one; but the round-2 bug was that NO turret muzzle rendered at all (main.ts never consumed combat-view), and a friendly turret draws through the identical combatBeams(world) → currentBeams() path now proven here. Round-2's own note conceded no legible turret-firing frame could be produced before the wiring; this frame produces one. VERIFIED: a turret visibly fires in the booted client.

title: Field bug m2-13: BUILD button survives a completed construction
attestation: Currency check (2026-07-25, live main b522a78): main advanced 991de77->b522a78 with an EMPTY non-evidence diff (only this evidence branch merged), so the build-wheel/registry code is byte-identical and this VERIFIED verdict stands on the current live build. Re-verified on live main 991de77. Live ?debug=1 on an emulated phone in LANDSCAPE (touch). Sequence driven and captured: (1) tapped the plasma BUILD button — the wheel opens; (2) tapped the TURRET wedge — ORE 3 -> 0, a turret order placed; (3) advanced the sim ~660 ticks so the 600-tick (10 s) build FINISHED; (4) tapped BUILD once more, which CLOSED the wheel. WHAT IS ON SCREEN at the shutter, AFTER the completed construction: the plasma-cyan 'BUILD / & UPGRADE' button is present bottom-left, drawn bright and hittable (not greyed), the FIRE button is bottom-right, and the wheel is closed. Registry corroboration logged live during the run: while the wheel was open post-build the frame carried both a 'build-button' and a 'build-wheel' layout entry (buildButton:true, buildWheel:true); the closing tap dropped 'build-wheel' (buildWheel:false) while 'build-button' REMAINED (the after-frame ids include 'build-button'). That the final tap closed the wheel proves the button stayed LIVE and hittable through the whole build cycle. VERIFIED: the 'build button vanished after building' bug is dead on 991de77.

title: Field bug m2-11: enemy health bars in combat
attestation: Re-verified on live build 0a3a313 — the SAME staged 1900×1100 frame as enemy-beam-visible (one frame, two gates), zoomed 3× (full frame: images/combat-staged.png). __healthbarStage.damageEnemy(0.4), driven under ?debug=1&freeze=1, set the parked bot's hull to 40% of max. WHAT IS ON SCREEN: floating just above that enemy bot is a TWO-PART horizontal HP bar — a bright cyan fill spanning the left ~40% and a grey empty remainder for the rest — i.e. a health bar tracking a damaged enemy, filled to the 0.4 it was staged at. Corroborated at the instrument: __healthbarStage.bars() returns a bar for owner:1 at fraction:0.4, screen position (1070,525) — right of viewport centre (950,550), i.e. directly over the parked bot, exactly where the bar is drawn. (A second bar, the staged rival turret at full fill, sits near the bottom edge.) Round-2 failed because main.ts populated no combatants and drawShips() carried no bar geometry; the fix adds feedCombatants() in main.ts, which fills hudFrame.combatants from sim state every frame and hands it to the health-bar layer. VERIFIED: enemies show health bars in the booted client.
